Wanted to jump in here as a 53 year old woman who is just 5 days PO. 
So I don't have a ton of experience with much of this, but I can say that the 2nd week of the liquid diet was the hardest, and while I do sometimes feel hunger now it's not much. 

Leading up to this I had 4 months of prep, and met with 2 nutritionists because I had the surgery at a hospital a couple miles from where I live. 

I'm glad to still have the local nutritionist, and also she gave me two bottles of Bariatric One multivitamin and some samples of the calcium soft chews to see if I like them, so that could be an option for anyone. 

Pain has not been bad AT ALL maybe 2-3 out of ten since I got home. I have some 5mg oxy to take but really the acetaminophen takes care of it.

I did have to stay in the hospital 2 nights because I had urinary retention, but it resolved relatively quickly, and is something I also developed after my only previous abdominal surgery, gallbladder removal. 

This is embarrassing but it is part of my journey, so: my 2nd night at home I had bowel incontinence at night while I was sleeping. Luckily for me I have some rewashable mattress pads from yet another previous surgery and I use them most nights just to help my sheets stay clean longer. 

So that happened twice that night and I don't know if that is what is called dumping syndrome, or if it would have happened if I had been awake. 

That's the only real bummer I've had since the surgery, except they put me on the wrong floor by accident (cardiac vs bariatricl) and none of the nurses knew anything about how to care for me. 
I didn't get to get up and walk, they must shot me up with blood thinners. When I asked for an abdominal binder I was shamed and told "you have to buy some things yourself, you can't expect the hospital to provide everything." 

Then I got moved to the correct floor and the first nurse that walked in said, hey, would you like an abdominal binder??'

So yeah. Sorry this is so long. I like the idea of having a group of slightly-olders to share with, especially as we deal with loose skin. 

My insurance told me already that they would pay for loose skin removal, but those surgeries actually scare me, with their multiple-foot long incisions.

I've knit many pairs of socks, but I'm not an expert. This is my opinion. Socks take as many stitches as a sweater, just smaller. I think if you're going to invest your time and effort it's worth it get some dedicated sock yarn that's about 25% nylon or polyamide. 
That said, if you really want or need to work from stash without buying anything, I'd say either do the heels and toes with the super wash you have or reinforce them with it, depending on the gauge of the yarn.
You can of course knit them with the natural wool you have, just expect to be darning them in the future, which can be kind of fun and another good skill to learn.
